CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Pekalongan.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Pekalongan.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution of the City of Pekalongan which is positioned as an element of regional government administration.
5. Regional Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and DPRD in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
7. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
10. Implementation of Protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the relevant SKPD.
11. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
12. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
13. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which include and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
14. Victims of gender-based violence are people who because of their gender experience physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
15. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or fainting and/or causes death.
16. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
17. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
18. Victims of acts of violence are individuals or groups of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
21. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
22. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organization (NGO) that provides assistance.
23. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs.
24. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.
25. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
26. Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of victims of gender-based violence and children.
27. Safe house is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
28. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
29. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
30. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PEKALONGAN CITY
NUMBER 5 OF 2015
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR
VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILD VICTIMS

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb and damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security. This is philosophically stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire Nation and the Homeland of Indonesia. Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obligated to fulfill these provisions.

Human Rights states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government. Through Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, the government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent human rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation. To fulfill the Right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. Protection from violence that threatens their safety and health must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, and education that is appropriate to their physical and psychological development.

In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents are obligated to understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and legal apparatus that defend the interests of children is necessary for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled on defending the best interest of the child is needed to realize protection that is legal in nature. Furthermore, it is not uncommon to find cases of women and children who experience problems of physical, psychological, sexual and social violence. For example, women and children who are victims of assault, neglect, eviction and abuse by parents or others. For women and children who experience these problems, the government must provide a Safe House (children protection home) or Integrated Service Center (PPT) for women and children victims of violence. The Safe House or PPT is a safe place and is friendly in nature for women and children. The PPT is equipped with assistants/support personnel from educators, doctors, psychologists, religious leaders and networked with lawyers for women and children as well as the RPK Unit at the Police.

The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the government. The large number of cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low levels of economy, education, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, local governments can establish an Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) as a center for empowering women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of women and children victims of violence. From the framework above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children. From these various efforts, a legal framework will be realized in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and child victims.

Article 11
In order to provide services and protection against gender-based violence and violence against children, the Regional Government establishes the Women, Children and Adolescent Protection Institution (LP PAR) as an integrated service center for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children.

CHAPTER V
DUTIES AND AUTHORITIES OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT
Article 10
(1) The Regional Government has the duty to implement efforts to prevent the occurrence of gender-based and child violence, in the form of: a. collecting data and information about acts of gender-based and child violence, and laws and regulations; b. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the implementation of protection against acts of gender-based and child violence;
c. conducting education about anti-violence values toward gender and children; and
d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of protection against acts of gender-based and child violence.
(2) The Regional Government in anticipating the occurrence of acts of gender-based and child violence, has the authority to provide and organize services for victims in the form of: a. providing and facilitating the establishment of integrated services for victims of acts of violence by involving institutions and community elements;
b. encouraging community awareness of the importance of protection for victims; and
c. conducting community empowerment for the prevention of acts of violence; and
d. actively carrying out handling efforts for victims of gender-based and child violence.
(3) The Regional Government in implementing obligations as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) must pay attention to the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands, wives, or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.

Article 8
(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 6 letter b, shall be implemented in the form of community participation.
(2) The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. preventing the occurrence of gender-based and child violence;
b. providing information and/or reporting gender-based and child violence to law enforcement or authorized parties; and/or
c. participating in providing assistance, protection or handling of victims of gender-based and child violence.
(3) The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Sixth Part
Services for Victims of Acts of Violence

Part Eight
Empowerment of Victims of Acts of Violence

CHAPTER X
REPORTING
Article 29
(1) SKPD is obligated to report the implementation of protection services against gender-based violence and violence against children to the Mayor.
(2) Reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted in writing, covering:
a. administration;
b. finance;
c. services; and
d. performance.
(3) Submission of written reports on case recapitulation that are reported shall be conducted at least once every 3 (three) months.

Article 25
(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with stakeholders in the implementation of protection against gender-based and child violence.
(2) The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1), is carried out through:
  a. notification of employment opportunity information for victims of gender-based and child violence;
  b. education and training for victims of violence;
  c. educational assistance for victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
  d. fostering and increasing the economic independence of victims of violence.
(3) The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), shall be set forth in the form of an agreement.

Article 13
(1) The Women, Children and Adolescent Protection Institution in carrying out its duties and functions may coordinate with the Sub-District Women, Children and Adolescent Protection Institution and competent parties in conducting efforts to prevent the occurrence of criminal acts of gender-based violence and violence against children.
(2) Further provisions regarding the mechanism for implementing prevention duties as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by the Mayor's Regulation.

Article 16
In addition to victims of gender-based violence and children, the forms of services and assistance organized by LP-PAR are also provided to Children in Conflict with the Law. In legal literature, it is mentioned that Children in conflict with the law are children who have reached the age of 12 (twelve) years but have not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years and are not yet married:
a. Who are suspected, alleged, charged, or sentenced for committing a criminal offense;
b. Who become victims of a criminal offense or who see and/or hear directly the occurrence of a criminal offense.
Children in conflict with the law can also be defined as children who are forced to come into contact with the criminal justice system because:
a. They are suspected, charged, or declared proven guilty of violating the law
b. They have become victims as a result of acts of legal violations committed by a person/group of persons/institution/state against them; or
c. They have seen, heard, felt, or known of an event of legal violation.
There are two categories of child behavior that cause them to come into conflict with the law:
a. Status Offence, namely child delinquent behavior which if committed by adults is not considered a crime, for example: skipping school, running away from home, etc.
b. Juvenile Delinquency, namely child delinquent behavior which if committed by adults is considered a crime or criminal act, for example: robbery, rape, sexual harassment, etc. Therefore, if viewed from its scope, children in conflict with the law can be divided into:
a. Perpetrators or suspects of criminal offenses;
b. Victims of criminal offenses;
c. Witnesses to a criminal offense.
As a child, legal mechanisms and the sense of justice in society must be placed within a framework that constructively encourages their physical and psychological development.
The forms of services and assistance organized by LP-PAR are also provided to women in conflict with the law.
Legal protection of women's interests in performing their position in society requires the preparation of various laws and regulations, and the consistent enforcement thereof, as well as socialization activities to raise awareness of their rights and obligations. In addition, non-legal support is needed, because law is only one means of social control. Action agendas from various components of society in an integrative manner need and must be immediately realized.
Furthermore, in the context of empowerment and protection of women, there needs to be legal, psychological, social and economic assistance when women are faced with legal processes.

CHAPTER VIII
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 26
(1) The Regional Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection against gender-based violence and violence against children.
(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), includes: a. minimum service standards (SPM);
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
(3) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), is conducted with the principles of:
a. professional;
b. transparent; and
c. accountable.
(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for guidance and supervision by the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (2) and paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

MAYOR OF PEKALONGAN
DECIDES:
To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND VIOLENCE AGAINST CHILDREN.

Fourth Part
Services and Assistance

3.2.rationale: In the Indonesian source, the only explicit police-related reference is in the Penjelasan Umum: the integrated service center (PPT) is “berjaringan dengan … Unit RPK di Kepolisian” (networked with the RPK Unit at the Police). The Perda’s operative articles focus on establishing LP-PAR (Pasal 11) and do not mandate that the police must establish/operate a specialised VAW unit. A mere statement that services are networked with an existing police unit is not the same as a policy requirement to create a specialised police service unit. Therefore a “Yes” golden label (implying the policy establishes/requires a specialised police unit) appears incorrect; the judge’s “No” is consistent with the Indonesian text.

5.3.evaluator_rationale: The policy includes community participation through fostering local wisdom in handling cases, which reflects engagement with customary/cultural mechanisms in implementation.

5.3.rationale: The Indonesian text explicitly includes cultural/traditional elements in implementation via community participation. Pasal 28 ayat (3) huruf f states: “menumbuhkan kearifan lokal dengan prinsip non diskriminasi dan kepentingan terbaik bagi korban…”. This is an explicit instruction to foster/use local wisdom (kearifan lokal), which is a form of engaging cultural/traditional mechanisms or norms in handling cases. Given that this language is present in the operative provisions, a golden label of “No” (no traditional/cultural engagement) appears wrong; the judge’s “Yes” matches the Indonesian text.

b. They have become victims as a result of acts of legal violations committed by a person/group of persons/institution/state against them; or
c. They have seen, heard, felt, or known of an event of legal violation.
There are two categories of child behavior that cause them to come into conflict with the law:
a. Status Offence, namely child delinquent behavior which if committed by adults is not considered a crime, for example: skipping school, running away from home, etc.
b. Juvenile Delinquency, namely child delinquent behavior which if committed by adults is considered a crime or criminal act, for example: robbery, rape, sexual harassment, etc. Therefore, if viewed from its scope, children in conflict with the law can be divided into:
a. Perpetrators or suspects of criminal offenses;
b. Victims of criminal offenses;
c. Witnesses to a criminal offense.
As a child, legal mechanisms and the sense of justice in society must be placed within a framework that constructively encourages their physical and psychological development.
The forms of services and assistance organized by LP-PAR are also provided to women in conflict with the law.
Legal protection of women's interests in performing their position in society requires the preparation of various laws and regulations, and the consistent enforcement thereof, as well as socialization activities to raise awareness of their rights and obligations. In addition, non-legal support is needed, because law is only one means of social control. Action agendas from various components of society in an integrative manner need and must be immediately realized.
Furthermore, in the context of empowerment and protection of women, there needs to be legal, psychological, social and economic assistance when women are faced with legal processes.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Pekalongan.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Pekalongan.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution of the City of Pekalongan which is positioned as an element of regional government administration.
5. Regional Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and DPRD in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
7. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
10. Implementation of Protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the relevant SKPD.
11. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
12. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
13. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which include and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
14. Victims of gender-based violence are people who because of their gender experience physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
15. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or fainting and/or causes death.
16. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
17. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
18. Victims of acts of violence are individuals or groups of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
21. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
22. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organization (NGO) that provides assistance.
23. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs.
24. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.
25. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
26. Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of victims of gender-based violence and children.
27. Safe house is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
28. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
29. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
30. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.

CHAPTER V
DUTIES AND AUTHORITIES OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT
Article 10
(1) The Regional Government has the duty to implement efforts to prevent the occurrence of gender-based and child violence, in the form of: a. collecting data and information about acts of gender-based and child violence, and laws and regulations; b. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the implementation of protection against acts of gender-based and child violence;
c. conducting education about anti-violence values toward gender and children; and
d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of protection against acts of gender-based and child violence.
(2) The Regional Government in anticipating the occurrence of acts of gender-based and child violence, has the authority to provide and organize services for victims in the form of: a. providing and facilitating the establishment of integrated services for victims of acts of violence by involving institutions and community elements;
b. encouraging community awareness of the importance of protection for victims; and
c. conducting community empowerment for the prevention of acts of violence; and
d. actively carrying out handling efforts for victims of gender-based and child violence.
(3) The Regional Government in implementing obligations as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) must pay attention to the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands, wives, or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.

Article 8
(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 6 letter b, shall be implemented in the form of community participation.
(2) The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. preventing the occurrence of gender-based and child violence;
b. providing information and/or reporting gender-based and child violence to law enforcement or authorized parties; and/or
c. participating in providing assistance, protection or handling of victims of gender-based and child violence.
(3) The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER VI

Part One
Institutional

Article 11
In order to provide services and protection against gender-based violence and violence against children, the Regional Government establishes the Women, Children and Adolescent Protection Institution (LP PAR) as an integrated service center for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children.
